'''Achim Müller''' (14 February 1938 – 28 February 2024) was a German [[inorganic chemist]]. Mainly as a professor at [[Bielefeld University]],<ref>{{cite web | title=Achim Müller Bielefeld | website=Bielefeld University | url=https://wwwhomes.uni-bielefeld.de/chemie/ehemalig/ac1-mueller/ | language=de | access-date=23 July 2023}}
</ref> he contributed extensively to the chemistry of [[molybdenum]] oxides and sulfides. He died on 28 February 2024, at the age of 86.<ref>{{cite web |title=Achim Müller (1938 – 2024) |url=https://www.chemistryviews.org/achim_muller_1938_2024/ |website=Chemistry Views |date=10 March 2024 |access-date=10 March 2024}}</ref>

==Research contributions==
===Oxide clusters===
In the area of [[polyoxometalate]]s,<ref>Polyoxometalate Chemistry: An Old Field with New Dimensions in Several Disciplines, M. T. Pope, A. Müller, ''Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. Engl.'', 1991, 30, 34.</ref> he claimed to have identified the structure of one form of [[molybdenum blue]].<ref>Soluble [[Molybdenum blue]]s - "des Pudels Kern", A. Müller, C. Serain, ''Acc. Chem. Res.'', 2000, 33, 2.</ref><ref>a) A Nanosized Molybdenum Oxide Wheel with a Unique Electronic-Necklace Structure: STM Study with Submolecular Resolution, D. Zhong, F. L. Sousa, A. Müller, L. Chi, H. Fuchs, ''Angew. Chem. Int. Ed.'', 2011, 50, 7018; b) From Scheele and Berzelius to Müller: Polyoxometalates (POMs) revisited and the "missing link" between the bottom up and top down approaches, P. Gouzerh, [[Michel Che|M. Che]], [http://www.uni-bielefeld.de/chemie/emeriti/ac1-mueller/AMU/actualite.pdf ''l’actualité chimique''], 2006, June Issue, No. 298, 9.</ref> 

His later research related mainly to the synthesis of spherical porous metal oxide [[nanocapsules]] Mo<sub>132</sub> [[Coordination_cage#Keplerates|Keplerates]].<ref name="ref1-a">{{cite journal |last1=Müller |first1=Achim |last2=Gouzerh |first2=Pierre |title=From linking of metal-oxide building blocks in a dynamic library to giant clusters with unique properties and towards adaptive chemistry |journal=Chemical Society Reviews |date=2012 |volume=41 |issue=22 |pages=7431–63 |doi=10.1039/C2CS35169B |pmid=22948798 }}</ref><ref name="ref1-b">{{cite journal |last1=Müller |first1=Achim |last2=Gouzerh |first2=Pierre |title=Capsules with Highly Active Pores and Interiors: Versatile Platforms at the Nanoscale |journal=Chemistry - A European Journal |date=22 April 2014 |volume=20 |issue=17 |pages=4862–4873 |doi=10.1002/chem.201305010 |pmid=24644235 |bibcode=2014ChEuJ..20.4862M }}</ref><ref name="ref2-a">{{cite journal |last1=Müller |first1=Achim |last2=Reuter |first2=Hans |last3=Dillinger |first3=Stephan |title=Supramolecular Inorganic Chemistry: Small Guests in Small and Large Hosts |journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition in English |date=17 November 1995 |volume=34 |issue=21 |pages=2328–2361 |doi=10.1002/anie.199523281 }}</ref><ref name="ref2-b">{{cite journal |last1=DAY |first1=VICTOR W. |last2=KLEMPERER |first2=WALTER G. |last3=YAGHI |first3=OMAR M. |title=Induced molecule self-organization |journal=Nature |date=July 1991 |volume=352 |issue=6331 |pages=115–116 |doi=10.1038/352115c0 |bibcode=1991Natur.352..115D |s2cid=45122433 }}</ref><ref name="ref2-c">{{cite journal |last1=Müller |first1=A. |title=Supramolecular inorganic species: An expedition into a fascinating, rather unknown land mesoscopia with interdisciplinary expectations and discoveries |journal=Journal of Molecular Structure |date=September 1994 |volume=325 |issue=1 |pages=13–35 |doi=10.1016/0022-2860(94)80014-6 |bibcode=1994JMoSt.325...13M }}</ref><ref name="ref2-d">{{cite journal |last1=Rohmer |first1=Marie-Madeleine |last2=Bénard |first2=Marc |last3=Blaudeau |first3=Jean-Philippe |last4=Maestre |first4=Juan-M |last5=Poblet |first5=Josep-M |title=From Lindqvist and Keggin ions to electronically inverse hosts |journal=Coordination Chemistry Reviews |date=December 1998 |volume=178-180 |pages=1019–1049 |doi=10.1016/S0010-8545(98)00162-3 }}</ref> He also investigated [[isopolyoxovanadate]]s has provided some of the most instructive examples of host-guest inorganic chemistry, leading to the recognition that a [[polyoxometalate]] is a supramolecular species involving a negatively charged host cage and a negatively charged encapsulated guest, and hence opening a new era in polyoxometalate chemistry. The template self-organization of an ”electronically inverse host” around a negatively charged guest might seem somewhat puzzling: According to theoretical studies, this follows from the fact that electrostatic repulsion is overcome by maximizing the molecular electrostatic potential at the guest.

===Sulfides===
Müller also reported many new types of [[transition metal]] sulphur compounds.<ref name="ref2-a" /><ref name="ref2-b" /><ref name="ref2-c" /><ref name="ref2-d" />

== Academic career ==
Achim Müller studied [[chemistry]] and [[physics]] at the [[University of Göttingen]] and received there his PhD degree (1965) and the Habilitation (1967). In 1971, he became professor at the [[University of Dortmund]] and in 1977 professor of [[Inorganic Chemistry]] at [[Bielefeld University]]. In 2006 he was awarded the Manchot-Forschungsprofessur of the [[Technical University of Munich]].  

== Personal life==
Müller enjoyed ancient Greek philosophy, classical music, and mountain hiking. He had a passion for woodland birds from his early childhood, a pastime which his father cherished also.  In his professional life, he was attentive to recognition.<ref>Like Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung, Die Welt, Süddeutsche Zeitung, Neue Zürcher Zeitung, Handelsblatt, Göttinger Tagesblatt, The Hindu, El Pais, Gazeta Wyborcza, Situs Kimia Indonesia, Times of India, Science in Siberia, Scientific American, American Mathematical Society, New Scientist, Chemistry World, Chemistry in Britain, Materials Today, Spektrum der Wissenschaft, Bild der Wissenschaft, Naturwissenschaftliche Rundschau, Chem. i. u. Zeit, La Recherche, Der Spiegel. For details see [http://www.uni-bielefeld.de/chemie/emeriti/ac1-mueller/] and Reference 6 c) [http://www.uni-bielefeld.de/chemie/emeriti/ac1-mueller/AMU/chemieaesthetik.pdf ''Mitteilungen'']</ref>
